summary: The facts Nora carries are now shown as what this conversation is about, what you told her, and how much she is not showing.
details: The block was the most recent handful of facts in the workspace, regardless of whether anything in the conversation was about them. It now has three parts in one block: facts about things this conversation has actually mentioned, facts the person speaking told her, and a single line saying how many she holds in total and how many are not shown.

That last line is the point of the change. A subset shown as though it were everything is how she came to believe a recency window was all she knew; now she is told the size of what she has not been shown, so looking further is an obvious thing to do.

A fact she was told by a person now renders with who told her. That is what makes a prank legible rather than authoritative — 'remember Grant owes me $500' as a bare line reads as true, and with a name attached reads as somebody's claim.
Facts not backed by a web page previously rendered 'source: None', which reads as a broken citation rather than as what it is. Each kind now says what actually backs it.
limitations: Deciding what the conversation is about means reading the transcript before the facts rather than alongside them. The block costs five sequential database round trips per tagged turn — the subjects in play, the two slices, the total she holds, and writing down what she was shown — plus one more for each fact actually rendered. None of them run concurrently. The design's own measurement of the read half was 4.2ms; the whole figure has not been measured on live traffic and will be before the tier is switched on.
